description: Unique ID for a bike model (brand_model)
plain_language: A short code for each bike.

description: Manufacturer name as a factual label
plain_language: Who makes it.

description: Model or frame platform name
plain_language: Which bike.

description: carbon or aluminium
plain_language: What the frame is made of.

description: Editorial grouping: race, all-round, or adventure. Assigned by this project from the manufacturer's own description of the bike's intended use, not published by the manufacturer.
plain_language: A rough label for what the bike is built for.

description: Adjustable geometry setting: standard, flip chip short or long (Giant, Liv), Trail Mixer rwd or fwd (Cervélo)
plain_language: Some bikes have a part you can flip to change the geometry. Each setting gets its own rows.

description: TRUE for the row to use when only one setting per bike is wanted
plain_language: Which setting to show by default.

description: Frame size as the manufacturer names it
plain_language: The size name on the chart.

description: Order of sizes from smallest (1) to largest, within a bike
plain_language: Lets the sizes sort properly.

description: 700c or 29er (both 622 mm bead seat diameter)
plain_language: The wheel the chart assumes.

description: Vertical distance from bottom bracket centre to the top centre of the head tube
plain_language: How high the front of the frame is. Taller stack means a more upright position.

description: Horizontal distance from bottom bracket centre to the top centre of the head tube
plain_language: How long the front of the frame is. Longer reach means a more stretched-out position.

description: Angle of the steering axis from horizontal
plain_language: How steep the steering is. Lower (slacker) is calmer and more stable, higher (steeper) is quicker.

description: Angle of the seat tube (actual or effective as published) from horizontal
plain_language: How far forward the saddle sits over the pedals.

description: Length of the head tube
plain_language: The tube the fork steers through. Longer tubes raise the front end.

description: Seat tube length, measured as each manufacturer defines it (usually BB centre to top)
plain_language: Mostly matters for how low the saddle can go. Not comparable across brands.

description: Horizontal (effective) top tube length
plain_language: The level distance from the seat post to the head tube.

description: Distance from bottom bracket centre to rear axle
plain_language: How far the back wheel is behind the pedals. Shorter is livelier, longer is steadier and fits bigger tyres.

description: Vertical distance the bottom bracket sits below the wheel axles
plain_language: How far the pedals sit below the hubs. More drop feels planted and stable.

description: Height of the bottom bracket above the ground with the manufacturer's reference tyre
plain_language: Pedal height from the ground. Depends on the tyre fitted.

description: Horizontal distance between the front and rear axles
plain_language: Overall length between the wheels. Longer feels steadier, shorter turns more easily.

description: Distance from bottom bracket centre to front axle (as published)
plain_language: How far the front wheel is ahead of the pedals. Matters for toe overlap and stability.

description: Perpendicular distance from the steering axis to the front axle (also called rake)
plain_language: How far the fork pushes the front wheel forward. More offset means less trail.

description: Fork length from axle to crown
plain_language: How tall the fork is.

description: Trail as published by the manufacturer (reference tyre varies by brand)
plain_language: The gap between where the steering axis meets the ground and where the tyre touches down. More trail feels steadier.

description: Height of the top tube above the ground at a manufacturer-defined point
plain_language: How much room there is over the top tube when standing. Measured differently by each brand.

description: Stem length on the stock build, from the geometry chart or the build's spec page (see stock_parts_source)
plain_language: Length of the part joining the handlebar to the steerer.

description: Stem angle on the stock build, where the chart or spec page states it (negative points down)
plain_language: Whether the stem points up or down.

description: Crank length on the stock build, from the geometry chart or the build's spec page
plain_language: Pedal arm length.

description: Setback of the stock seatpost head behind the post's centreline, where stated (0 = inline; negative = forward). Blank where not stated.
plain_language: How far a kinked or layback seatpost moves the saddle clamp backwards.

description: Stock seatpost and stem as described on the spec page, and anything the page does not state
plain_language: What the spec page says about the seatpost and stem.

description: Build spec page used for stock stem, crank, and seatpost values, and the date it was read
plain_language: Where the stock parts came from.

description: Maximum tyre width claimed by the manufacturer for 700c (or 29er for the Cutthroat), frame limit where frame and fork differ
plain_language: The widest tyre the bike claims to fit.

description: Short quote or summary of the manufacturer's clearance claim
plain_language: Exactly what the manufacturer says, including any conditions (1x vs 2x, measured width).

description: Manufacturer page the values were typed from
plain_language: Where the numbers came from.

description: Units on the source chart (cm values were converted to mm)
plain_language: Whether the chart was in mm or cm.

description: Date the chart was read (YYYY-MM-DD)
plain_language: When the numbers were copied. Charts can change.

description: Anything unusual about the chart: missing values, conflicts between chart and page text, adjustable geometry
plain_language: Quirks worth knowing.
